allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.category_profile: Ready-to-eat breakfast cereals: kids, family, adult and specialty cereals, granola and muesli, boxed or bagged.
attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.

allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.category_profile: Ready-to-eat breakfast cereals: kids, family, adult and specialty cereals, granola and muesli, boxed or bagged.
attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.category_profile: Ready-to-eat breakfast cereals: kids, family, adult and specialty cereals, granola and muesli, boxed or bagged.
attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.

allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.category_profile: Ready-to-eat breakfast cereals: kids, family, adult and specialty cereals, granola and muesli, boxed or bagged.
attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

Grainbowl Classic Toasted Grain Puffs pack airy, oven-toasted rounds into a 27 oz resealable bag built for households that refill their cereal bowl more than once a week. Each puff is baked light and crisp, offering a clean crunch without a heavy, syrupy coating, so the flavor stays simple and the texture stays satisfying all the way to the last spoonful. allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat

allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. {"SZ_ITEM": "16 OZ", "brand": "MORNINGFIELD CEREAL CO", "category": "RTE CEREAL", "comm": "ALL-FAMILY RTE CEREAL", "dis_name": "Morningfield Cereal Co Vanilla Almond Flakes Family Cereal", "ingredients": "Whole Grain Oats, Corn Meal, Rice, Malt Flavor, Vitamin B12. Vitamins And Minerals: Reduced Iron, Contains 2% Or Less Of Salt, Folic Acid, Oat Bran, Sugar, Almonds, Vitamin B1 (Thiamin Hydrochloride), Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin), Corn Syrup, Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine Hydrochloride), Niacinamide.", "lifestyles": "SNAP EBT eligible, Whole grain", "long_desc": "Morningfield Cereal Co brings a cheerful bowl to the table with crisp flakes toasted from whole grain oats and corn meal, finished with sliced almonds and a splash of natural vanilla. Every member of the house can scoop a bowlful for breakfast or grab a handful as an after-school bite. The nutty crunch pairs easily with cold milk, a favorite plant-based pour, or a spoonful stirred into yogurt for the little ones who like to build their own mix. Parents like that the box keeps its crunch from the first pour to the last, and kids like the toasty vanilla sweetness that makes mornings easier to get moving. Pack it in a lunchbox baggie, top a bowl of fruit with it, or just eat it dry on a busy afternoon - this flaky blend fits wherever your family schedule takes you. One resealable box holds enough for the whole crew to share across the week, no fuss, no sorting through picky opinions.


- CRISP AND NUTTY: Toasted oat and corn flakes mixed with real almond pieces and vanilla flavor for a crunch everyone enjoys

- FAMILY FRIENDLY: Mild sweetness and easy crunch make this a cereal both grown-ups and kids reach for

{"SZ_ITEM": "22OZ", "brand": "IRONVALE BREAD CO", "category": "BREADS", "comm": "BREAD - HARD VARIETY", "dis_name": "Ironvale Bread Co Sprouted Whole Grain Organic Loaf, Unsliced", "ingredients": "Organic Whole Wheat (Organic Sprouted Whole Wheat Flour, Organic Cracked Whole Wheat), Water, Organic Cane Sugar, Organic Oat Fiber, Organic Cultured Wheat Flour, Yeast, Organic Vinegar, Organic Expeller Pressed Sunflower Oil, Enzymes, Organic Sprouted Grain Mix (Organic Sprouted Wheat, Organic Sprouted Barley), Contains 2% or Less of Each of the Following: Organic Molasses, Organic Whole Wheat Flour, Organic Rolled Oats, Sea Salt, Organic Wheat Gluten, Organic Acerola Cherry Powder.", "lifestyles": "SNAP EBT eligible, Whole grain", "long_desc": "Ironvale Bread Co bakes this whole loaf with organic sprouted grains for a hearty texture and a mild, nutty flavor. allowed_values.definition: Puffs are light, airy cereal pieces that are typically round or irregularly shaped, made from puffed grains such as corn or rice, and are characterized by their crispy texture and often sweet flavor. Unlike other cereal forms like flakes or clusters, puffs do not have a flat or dense structure, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Puffs

allowed_values.definition: Granola & Muesli refers to a type of cereal that typically consists of a mixture of rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits, often sweetened and baked into clusters or served loose, distinguishing it from other cereal forms like flakes or puffs by its chewy texture and wholesome ingredients.
allowed_values.name: Granola & Muesli

allowed_values.definition: Flakes are thin, flat pieces of cereal typically made from grains, characterized by their crisp texture and often used in breakfast cereals. Unlike puffs or clusters, flakes are not formed into rounded shapes or clumped together, making them distinct in both texture and appearance.
allowed_values.name: Flakes

allowed_values.definition: Crisps are a type of cereal characterized by their light, airy texture and often irregular shapes, typically produced through a process that involves puffing or baking grains. Unlike flakes or clusters, crisps are generally more fragile and provide a distinct crunch when consumed.
allowed_values.name: Crisps

allowed_values.definition: Clusters refer to cereal pieces that are formed by binding together grains, nuts, or other ingredients into larger, cohesive chunks, distinguishing them from loose or flaked cereal forms. This form is characterized by its crunchy texture and is often found in granola or specialty cereals.
allowed_values.name: Clusters

allowed_values.definition: Shredded refers to cereal that is made from finely shredded pieces of grain, typically wheat, resulting in a texture that is light and airy, often used in biscuit-shaped cereal products. This form is distinct from other cereal forms such as flakes or clusters, which have different textures and shapes.
allowed_values.name: Shredded

allowed_values.definition: Porridge is a hot cereal made from oats or other grains that are cooked in water or milk until they reach a creamy, thick consistency. It is distinct from other cereal forms like granola or flakes, which are typically dry and crunchy.
allowed_values.name: Porridge

allowed_values.definition: Assorted refers to a collection of different cereal types or flavors packaged together, providing a variety of options within a single product, distinguishing it from single-type cereals.
allowed_values.name: Assorted

attributes.category_profile: Ready-to-eat breakfast cereals: kids, family, adult and specialty cereals, granola and muesli, boxed or bagged.
attributes.definition: Cereal Form describes the physical shape, texture, or processing style of a cereal product, such as puffs, flakes, clusters, or granola. This attribute helps distinguish products based on their structural characteristics rather than flavor or ingredient composition.

allowed_values.definition: The "Multiple" value indicates that the cereal is made from a combination of different grains or sources, rather than a single grain type, reflecting a blend of various cereal sources in its formulation.
allowed_values.name: Multiple

allowed_values.definition: Oat refers to the grain derived from the Avena sativa plant, commonly used in cereals and other food products, characterized by its high fiber content and nutritional benefits. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn, which have different properties and uses.
allowed_values.name: Oat

allowed_values.definition: Corn is a cereal grain derived from the plant Zea mays, characterized by its yellow kernels and commonly used as a primary ingredient in various breakfast cereals, providing a sweet flavor and crunchy texture. It is distinct from other grains like wheat or oats, which have different flavor profiles and textures.
allowed_values.name: Corn

allowed_values.definition: Wheat is a cereal grain that serves as a primary ingredient in various food products, characterized by its high carbohydrate content and nutritional value, particularly in the form of whole grain. It is distinct from other grains like rice or corn, which have different nutritional profiles and culinary uses.
allowed_values.name: Wheat

allowed_values.definition: Rice is a cereal grain that is primarily cultivated for human consumption, characterized by its small, oval-shaped grains that are typically white, brown, or black in color. It serves as a staple food in many cultures and is distinct from other grains like wheat or corn due to its unique texture and cooking properties.
allowed_values.name: Rice

allowed_values.definition: Specialty refers to cereals made from unique or less common grains or blends that are often marketed for their health benefits or distinctive flavors, distinguishing them from mainstream cereals that primarily use common grains like wheat or corn.
allowed_values.name: Specialty

allowed_values.definition: Flaxseed refers to the seeds of the flax plant, which are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and fiber, and are often used as a key ingredient in cereals for their nutritional benefits. Unlike other cereal sources, flaxseed is specifically recognized for its high content of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and is typically ground or milled to enhance digestibility.
allowed_values.name: Flaxseed

allowed_values.definition: Bran refers to the hard outer layers of cereal grains, particularly wheat, that are rich in dietary fiber and nutrients. It is distinct from other grain components such as endosperm and germ, and is commonly used in cereals to enhance fiber content.
allowed_values.name: Bran

allowed_values.definition: Quinoa is a gluten-free, whole grain seed that is high in protein and fiber, commonly used in cereals and health foods, and distinguished from other grains by its unique nutritional profile and origin as a traditional crop of the Andes.
allowed_values.name: Quinoa

allowed_values.definition: Chia refers to the seeds of the Salvia hispanica plant, which are used as a primary ingredient in cereals, known for their high nutritional value, including omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and protein. Products labeled as "Chia" must contain chia seeds as a significant component, distinguishing them from other grain sources.
allowed_values.name: Chia

allowed_values.definition: Hemp refers to cereal products made primarily from hemp seeds, which are known for their high nutritional value, including protein, healthy fats, and essential amino acids. This distinguishes it from other cereal sources like wheat or oats, which do not share the same nutritional profile.
allowed_values.name: Hemp

allowed_values.definition: Buckwheat is a gluten-free pseudocereal derived from the seeds of the buckwheat plant, commonly used in various cereal products and known for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value, distinguishing it from traditional grains like wheat and oats.
allowed_values.name: Buckwheat
